target.title: refactor(plugins): trim path safety facade
target.body:
Related: #105595

## What Problem This Solves

The unused-export ratchet still carried ten plugin-local path-safety aliases that no plugin code imports.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove only the redundant aliases from the internal plugin facade, retain the four helpers with real plugin consumers, and regenerate the full Knip baseline against the latest `main`.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior or public API change. Ten dead plugin-local exports leave the ratchet; current-main and Linux scan drift leave the regenerated baseline one entry smaller at 5,526.

## Evidence

- Exact Linux reconciliation: the CI scan identified five platform-specific required entries after the macOS regeneration; the committed 5,526-entry baseline is sorted, duplicate-free, and has SHA-256 `b37a9060ffcf3cc2fc6afb03c89728fd0220ec1ebff6dc2947368aa12fd0b39a`.
- Touched-surface gate: `pnpm check:changed` passed, including formatting, plugin SDK API baseline, core and test typechecks, lint, package guards, database-first guards, import cycles, and webhook/pairing guards.
- Fresh final branch autoreview: clean, no actionable findings (0.94 confidence).
- Exact-head Linux ratchet passed: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29221265572/job/86726728210. Every other completed shard passed except `check-guards`, which reports repo-wide max-LOC baseline drift only in unrelated files: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29221265572/job/86726728219.

## AI Assistance

- Assisted: yes.
- Transcript: not included pending author opt-in.
